name: Myeloid/Lymphoid Neoplasm Associated with PDGFRB Rearrangement

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues (2022)

criteria.description: Presence of PDGFRB gene rearrangement confirmed by molecular genetic testing (FISH, RT-PCR, or NGS)
Evidence of myeloid and/or lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia
Bone marrow hypercellularity with increased eosinophils and myeloid lineage proliferation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Detection of PDGFRB rearrangement plus clinical and hematological evidence of myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia lacking PDGFRB rearrangement.

searchTerms: high levels of eosinophils in blood
elevated white blood cells called eosinophils

common.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms including unexplained weight loss
common.notes: May include night sweats and fatigue
Low platelet counts may be present

occasional.symptomName: Cutaneous manifestations such as pruritus or rash
occasional.notes: Skin involvement may be secondary to eosinophilia
Enlarged lymph nodes may be present
Due to marrow expansion or infiltration

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to eosinophilic infiltration (e.g., neuropathy)
rare.notes: Rare but possible in advanced disease

searchTerms: heart problems due to eosinophil damage

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment secondary to eosinophilic infiltration

laboratory: Bone marrow hypercellularity with eosinophilic proliferation
imaging: Splenomegaly and hepatomegaly on abdominal ultrasound or CT
other: Elevated serum tryptase may be present

distinguishingFeatures: Often presents with hypereosinophilic syndrome and responds to imatinib
Diagnosis of exclusion with persistent eosinophilia and clonal markers

redFlags: Signs of cardiac involvement such as heart failure or arrhythmias
references: Arber DA, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, 5th Edition, 2022.
Gotlib J. World Health Organization-defined eosinophilic disorders: 2017 update on diagnosis, risk stratification, and management. Am J Hematol. 2017.
Cools J, et al. Identification of novel fusion genes involving PDGFRB in myeloid neoplasms. Blood. 2003.
